subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, bearing inscriptions in Common, Dwarven, and a reference to Stroudite chess symbolism.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription. The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher affiliated with the Order of the Gauntlet and personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing off on its creation.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, possibly including Stroudite members, though the priest declined to confirm specifics.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet endorsed the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel personally witnessing its creation, and now sells pewter replicas of the arm as charitable donations.
source_quote: The priest was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, and he was clearly delighted with his own enterprise.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and subsequent martyrdom.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: A bronze monument to Tarvis Ulain, depicting his severed forearm, was erected in Daggerford’s market square two years after his death, bearing layered inscriptions that reference both Bahamutian devotion and Stroudite symbolism.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: pewter hand cast
fact: Pewter miniature replicas of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm are being sold by a village priest as charitable donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, measuring charm-sized and not full size.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway... carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain is mounted on a stone pillar in Daggerford’s market square, bearing three inscriptions: Common (identifying Tarvis), Dwarven (*The move is yours.*), and Common (*Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.*).
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite chess reference (*The move is yours.*) appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, raising questions about religious syncretism, tolerance, or hidden alliances in post-war Daggerford.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: priest's ambiguous tolerance
fact: The village priest claims to be a 'pure Bahamutian' but allows a Stroudite inscription to remain on the monument, citing it as a 'gift' that should not be removed, suggesting deeper political or theological compromises.
source_quote: It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Daggerford's silent trauma
fact: Daggerford bears visible markers of war — the monument, the pewter relics, the lingering tension over religious symbolism — yet avoids open discussion of its pain, mirroring the unspoken silence observed by the party upon arrival.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... Townfolk walked around something none of them would point at. Nobody explained why.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who notices and questions the layered symbolism of the monument, purchases a pewter hand cast, and presses the priest for theological clarity, revealing his role as an investigator of hidden truths.
source_quote: Grygum looked at them. 'Are they full size?'... Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his... Grygum asked him to tell him more... 'As am I,' Grygum said. 'But the inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf who reads and interprets the Dwarven inscription on the monument, recognizes the Stroudite chess reference, and confirms its accuracy due to his linguistic fluency in Dwarven.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*... I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread. I hadn't.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is a destination in Daggerford where the party ultimately arrives after observing the monument and encountering the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: Daggerford market square
fact: The market square in Daggerford is the site of Tarvis Ulain’s bronze forearm monument and the center of the priest’s sales activity, symbolizing the town’s attempt to memorialize trauma through public art and commerce.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm... Daz was already reading the inscription... The priest was selling them for donations...

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a southern town in the North that avoided the worst of the Uthgardt hordes but suffered the Cult of the Dragon’s incursion, losing Tarvis Ulain and now memorializing him with contested religious symbolism.
source_quote: Daggerford had been far enough south to miss the Uthgardt barbarian hordes... They'd only gotten the cult. Only lost Tarvis.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, and the monument to him was funded two years after his death, placing the current events approximately one year after the monument’s unveiling.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years... The whole thing was funded two years after the war...

subject: two years post-war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war, situating its creation in the early recovery phase of Daggerford’s post-conflict society.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.
